title: Magnetosensitivity of amphibian morphological pigmentation is light- and eye-dependent and consistent with the radical pair mechanism
summary: Weak magnetic fields influence a wide range of biological processes, yet the underlying mechanisms are poorly understood. The radical pair mechanism (RPM), which involves quantum spin dynamics, is a leading hypothesis. Here we show that weak magnetic fields modulate morphological pigmentation -- specifically, the number of perioptic melanophores -- in Xenopus laevis tadpoles in a field-strength-dependent manner.
